I started grad school three years ago and, when I did, I made a concerted effort to be outgoing and make friends with all the grad students in the department. I'm typically quite reserved and prefer small groups or solo time, so it was a big change to start organizing events for dozens of people on the regular, but I learned a lot in the process. But, looking back, I don't think I'd do it again.

See, what I've gathered from feigning extroversion is that you take the shotgun approach to friendships: fire a wide spray and hope you hit something good. The problem in the case of a new place with a lot of things to "hit" is that the shotgun approach leads to a lot of lame hangers-on that are difficult to shake once you've "befriended" them; such was my predicament with the power lifter in our department who fancied himself strong rather than fat. Devoid of much personality by himself, most conversations with him consisted with repeated movie lines, "friendly" insults, and eventual physical pushing, basically making this person a cartoon bully with catchphrases. While I could not stand being near this person, he would be at all the social events I either planned or attended, presumably because no better options would ever come his way. I came in with a hatred of the overweight, but I can guarantee you this person redoubled my distaste for fat.

Over the past couple years, I've learned the folly of my attempt to be outgoing, instead hanging out with a few good friends rather than many meh friends. During this transition, I basically stopped talking to anyone fat in the department, which has dramatically improved the aesthetics of my friend group as well as my mood. The only problem being, I still have to see these fats at large department events, including the power lifter. After one such event, I was reminded of the story of the mayotanker that regained humanity after someone texted him "fat fuck" on a daily basis, and I vowed to try it on this particularly fat fucker.

The first message was received with "Woo what was that for," after which I told the fat fuck to lose weight. Every subsequent message has been met with silence. I've added statistics with links to articles in many texts, but no response. I was beginning to think it was a waste of time.

That is, until I saw him again in person. He couldn't make eye contact with me, wouldn't address me in a group conversation, would quickly leave when I walked up on a group he was in. And I love it.

Sure, he hasn't lost weight. But he's ashamed of himself, and that's all that matters to me. Plus, there's no way I have to hang out with him ever again. And continuing to send "fat fuck" via text takes literally no effort: I have an automatic text scheduler that does it for me, so cancelling it would take more work. I may have failed to chisel a human from this slab of fat, but I succeeded in improving my life, which is all I could have hoped for.

I have tasted victory, and it's so much sweeter than Beetus.
